conventions.convention: G is connected, simply connected and complex semisimple; X=G/B, with positive roots selected by B. The inherited Axiom of Choice is assumed.
O_X(η)=G×^B C_η=L_{-η}; the isotropy character of D_κ is κ+ρ, D_{-ρ} is ordinary differential operators, and χ_κ(z)=pr(z)(κ−ρ).
For complex κ, antidominance excludes positive integral pairings with every positive coroot; regularity excludes zero pairings with every coroot.
Left D_κ-modules are required to be quasi-coherent over O_X; coherence over D_κ means local finite presentation over D_κ, not O_X-coherence.
The Category O correspondence uses the exact central-character subcategory, annihilated by ker χ_κ, rather than the entire generalized-character block.

The partial-flag TDO D^α_{κ−ρ} has isotropy character κ. Ordinary differential inverse image has relative structure-sheaf factor; tensoring by O_X(ρ), of fiber degree −1, produces the singular D_κ-module.
The singular filtration assumes that the full zero-root subsystem is generated by its zero simple roots. Its fixed root sequence permits zero successive quotients and includes the empty sequence.

load_bearing.statement: For sufficiently dominant integral η, put L_η=O_X(−η) and V_η=Γ(X,L_η)*. For every quasi-coherent D_κ-module M, coevaluation M→M⊗L_η⊗V_η splits as sheaves of complex vector spaces for antidominant κ; evaluation M⊗V_η*→M⊗L_η splits for regular antidominant κ. The splittings are natural and commute with the diagonal U(g)-actions.

Assuming the flag setup and AC, for every complex κ the infinitesimal action induces a filtered algebra isomorphism A_κ→Γ(X,D_κ), where χ_κ(z)=pr(z)(κ−ρ). No dominance, regularity or integrality condition is imposed.
For antidominant κ, every quasi-coherent left D_κ-module M has H^i(X,M)=0 for i>0, and Γ(X,−) is exact. If κ is also regular, Γ(X,M)=0 implies M=0.
For an antidominant complex weight κ in a finite reduced crystallographic root system, κ−wκ is not in Q_+\{0} for every w∈W. If κ is also regular, κ−wκ is not in Q_+ for w≠1.

For complex antidominant κ whose full zero-root subsystem has simple system J, a chosen reduced expression of w_J gives fixed embeddings H_N⊂⋯⊂H_0 and E_N⊂⋯⊂E_0=D_κ⊗O_X(ρ). Each quotient E_{j−1}/E_j is O_X(ρ)⊗p_{α_j}^†N_j for a coherent partial-TDO module N_j, and E_N is generated by finitely many global differential sections.

On P¹, with L=O(−1) and D_0=Diff(L), every quasi-coherent D_0-module Q with Γ(Q)=0 is canonically L⊗Γ(L^{-1}⊗Q), with trivial sl₂-action on the second factor. The stated central-base and product-TDO versions classify relative kernel modules, preserve coherence under their stated hypotheses, and glue by natural evaluation.

For antidominant κ and a simple α with zero κ-coroot pairing, every coherent D_κ-module M has R^q p_{α*}M=0 for q>0. Moreover p_{α*}M=0 iff M≅O_X(ρ)⊗p_α^†N for a coherent D^α_{κ−ρ}-module N, canonically recovered by p_{α*}(O_X(−ρ)⊗M).

For regular antidominant κ, Loc_κ and Γ_κ are inverse equivalences between all left A_κ-modules and quasi-coherent left D_κ-modules, restricting to finitely generated A_κ-modules and coherent D_κ-modules.

concerns.concern: Step 2.1 concludes that Γ is not exact from nonzero R¹Γ computed in the category of all D_κ-module sheaves. The page convention restricts D_κ-modules to underlying quasi-coherent sheaves, whereas lem-pa36-module-global-sections-derived-cohomology establishes its comparison only in the full module-sheaf category. Nonexactness on that larger category alone does not establish nonexactness on the quasi-coherent subcategory. The conclusion is sound, but needs the short bridge, for example the quasi-coherent D-module sequence M→j_*(M|_U)→coker for a standard affine chart U; the middle term is acyclic and the nonzero H¹(M) forces failure of surjectivity on sections.

Verification 3.1 says, 'By [F4], global sections is not faithful and not exact at this translated twist.' Nonfaithfulness follows directly from the nonzero module with zero sections. For nonexactness on the stipulated quasi-coherent D-module category, F4 only compares cohomology with derived sections in all module sheaves. As in cex-pa36-positive-twist-global-sections-fail, supply the quasi-coherent affine-open direct-image sequence or an explicit restricted-category derived-functor comparison.

seams_checked.note: Read both page texts and the route-convention definition. Both use the published BGG Category O convention. The localization page explicitly treats this prerequisite as reading context and imports no KLR, Hecke, grading or multiplicity theorem. The route page makes no reverse localization claim that would strengthen the regular, integral or exact-central-character hypotheses.
